messages:
Carlos (Support): heads-up — getting multiple customer escalations from APAC on noticeably higher p95/p99 for the inference API since ~11:15 UTC. Example: customer 'PaperDesk' reported interactive UX stalls. I pulled a quick dashboard: ap-southeast-1 p95 from ~180ms to ~420ms, p99 jumped from ~900ms to ~2.1s. Error rate is stable, just latency.

Aisha (SRE): thanks — do we have traces? are spans showing where the time is spent (network vs server CPU)?

Carlos (Support): attaching a sample trace from the customer (redacted):
```
client -> edge-pop-sg -> tls-handshake(220ms) -> edge-proxy-accept(30ms) -> route-to-model(40ms) -> model-first-byte(10ms)
```
Most of the added time is in the TLS handshake and tcp connect.

Tom (Edge): interesting — that points at TLS + network between client and our POP rather than backend. I'm seeing increased SYN/TLS RTTs in our sg-pop metrics starting ~11:12. MTR from affected customer IP shows cross-az hop shift:
```
traceroute to pop.sg.redwood.net (198.51.100.23), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.1.1  1.2 ms
 2  203.19.45.1  4.3 ms
 3  203.19.46.2  5.1 ms
 4  203.19.60.9  7.8 ms  <--: change: now takes an extra ASN hop via transit-2
 5  198.51.100.23  120.4 ms  <-- big jump at last hop
```
That 120ms last hop is new — usually last hop is <15ms.

Priya (Networking): I pulled BGP/peering telemetry around that time — there was a transient route shift for a handful of prefixes to transit-2 (our backup peer) due to a flapping session with peer-primary. It looks like traffic for some customer prefixes got steered through a longer path. That matches high SYN/TLS RTT.

ops-alerts-bot: ALERT: pop-sg tcp_tls_rtt_p95 > 400ms (11:14 UTC)

Aisha (SRE): good find. Are TLS handshakes failing to resume? If session resumes are missed we'll pay full handshake cost each request. Tom, can you confirm whether session resumption was working for these clients?

Tom (Edge): we saw a small drop in TLS session ticket acceptance rate on sg-pop at the same time. Acceptance rate fell from 98% -> 63%. Looking into logs now.

Carlos (Support): customers report spikes are intermittent (couple mins) but that's enough to kill UX. Any quick mitigations we can do while Priya and infra sort peering?

Priya (Networking): short-term mitigations: (1) reduce DNS TTL for affected POPs to 30s so clients can re-resolve to alternate POPs quicker, (2) nudge traffic steering to prefer singapore-local paths that avoid transit-2 for those prefixes, (3) ask Edge to temporarily enable longer TLS session ticket lifetimes for reconnecting clients. Note: TTL change helps new connections only.

Tom (Edge): implementing (3) now — bumping session ticket lifetime + ensure tickets are rotated across replicas. Also enabling session resumption cache sticky to POP to avoid cross-pop cache misses. Rolling config to sg-pop in next 90s.

deploy-bot: Started config-rollout edge/ssl/session-ticket-lifetime -> sg-pop (rollout id: r-4821). 0/12 done.

Aisha (SRE): I'll apply a temporary traffic steering override to move affected prefixes to our singapore-primary peer (avoids transit-2) — applying now and will monitor p95. Doing a scoped reroute (10 min window) to test.

Leah (Product): notifying affected self-serve customers via status page? We should be transparent for those experiencing UX issues.

Carlos (Support): already posted a short note to status: "Intermittent higher latency for APAC users impacting p95/p99 — investigating routing/TLS connection impacts". Link: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/rlw-2026-03-apac-latency

Priya (Networking): update: peer-primary had a flapping session due to config mismatch on their side; they've confirmed and are rolling a fix. We still want to continue mitigations while their BGP stabilizes.

Tom (Edge): rollout finished: session ticket lifetime increased and cache sticky enabled. Observed immediate improvement in TLS acceptance rate from 63% -> 95% on sg-pop.

deploy-bot: rollout edge/ssl/session-ticket-lifetime -> sg-pop completed (12/12).

Aisha (SRE): reroute applied. observable p95 dropped from 420ms -> 195ms within ~2 minutes. p99 dropped from ~2.1s -> ~780ms. Still slightly above baseline but much better.

Priya (Networking): peer-primary finished maintenance and BGP is steady again; routes are converging back to optimal path. We should revert the temporary routing override once we confirm stability.

Carlos (Support): customers report improved responsiveness. PaperDesk confirms their UX lag went away after ~11:35 UTC.

Aisha (SRE): action items:
- Priya: keep monitoring BGP peering and confirm peer-primary stability (DONE? by 11:50 UTC) -> Priya (in progress)
- Tom: keep TLS ticket/cache config active for 24h, gather session acceptance metrics (due EOD) -> Tom (in progress)
- Carlos: follow up with affected customers with root-cause note + mitigation steps (by EOD) -> Carlos
- Leah: prepare a short postmortem blurb for status update once we have final RCA (by tomorrow noon) -> Leah

Priya (Networking): quick RCA notes: root cause = transient BGP session flap with peer-primary causing route failover to transit-2 for a subset of APAC prefixes. Consequence = longer network path + higher SYN/TLS RTT, compounded by a temporary drop in TLS session ticket acceptance (likely due to traffic landing on different POPs/missing ticket cache), which made each connection pay full handshake cost.

Aisha (SRE): longer-term mitigations proposed: (1) add health-check-aware BGP failover policy to prevent immediate switching to long-path peers on single flap, (2) increase TTL awareness in traffic steering so we avoid routing oscillation for short-lived BGP events, (3) make TLS session tickets/migration more robust across POP replicas, (4) improve observability: correlate TLS acceptance rate with p95 automatically.

Leah (Product): fine — please turn the proposed items into a short project request and priority list; we can budget in the next sprint. Also want a template customer-facing RCA.

Aisha (SRE): noted. I'll open an internal incident ticket with the timeline + metrics + suggested followups. Ticket: INC-2026-APAC-RTT.

Carlos (Support): closing the thread for now. If latency reappears or customers ping again, I will re-open. Thanks all for the quick turnaround. :raised_hands:
